newsitem.title: USA: NBA BASKETBALL - CAMPBELL FILLS IN FOR SHAQ, LEADS LAKERS PAST T'WOLVES.
newsitem.headline: NBA BASKETBALL - CAMPBELL FILLS IN FOR SHAQ, LEADS LAKERS PAST T'WOLVES.

text.p: Elden Campbell, playing centre after Shaquille O'Neal suffered his second strained knee in 10 days, had 21 points and nine rebounds as the Los Angeles Lakers beat the Minnesota Timberwolves 100-84 Wednesday.

O'Neal, who had missed two games and the All-Star Game with a strained right knee, suffered a strained left knee in the first quarter and did not return. Campbell and rookie Travis Knight split time in the pivot, as they did last week during O'Neal's absence. Campbell also blocked four shots.
"My teammates were looking for me down low and keeping me involved in the game," Campbell said.
"It was a big blow to find out Shaq would play only eight minutes," Lakers coach Del Harris said. "But the guys still played a normal game."
Eddie Jones scored 19 points and keyed a pair of spurts for the Lakers, who have won eight of their last nine games and dealt Minnesota its worst home loss of the season.
"I would like to sugar-coat it, but I can't," Minnesota coach Flip Saunders said. "We got our butts kicked. They whipped us pretty bad. We didn't seem mentally ready to play."

All-Star forwards Kevin Garnett and Tom Gugliotta scored 17 and 16 points, respectively, for the Timberwolves, who welcomed back Stephon Marbury from injury. The rookie guard, who missed eight games with a thigh bruise, had 13 points and eight assists.
O'Neal went down while battling for a rebound. He scored 12 points on 6-of-7 shooting.
Knight scored 11 points and Robert Horry added 11 along with 10 rebounds and eight assists for the Lakers.

In Charlotte, All-Star Game Most Valuable Player Glen Rice continued his year-long scoring surge with 27 points and Anthony Mason had 21 points, 18 rebounds and eight assists as the Hornets defeated the New Jersey Nets 113-100 for their fifth win in six games.
Vlade Divac added 18 points, a team-record 12 blocks and nine rebounds for the Hornets, who bounced back from a buzzer loss at Chicago on Tuesday and collected their fourth straight home win.
Kendall Gill scored 26 points and Kerry Kittles added 23 for New Jersey.
In Atlanta, Dikembe Mutombo had 22 points and 11 rebounds as the Hawks pulled away to their 20th straight home victory, 106-84 over the Toronto Raptors.
Mookie Blaylock recorded 19 points, 11 assists and eight rebounds and Christian Laettner added 19 points and 12 rebounds for the Hawks.
Atlanta is two wins from matching its franchise-record home winning streak and hosts the Chicago Bulls on Friday.
At Detroit, Grant Hill registered his fifth triple-double of the season as the Pistons held on for a 96-87 victory over the Orlando Magic.
Hill had 31 points, 10 rebounds and 10 assists for Detroit.
Nick Anderson had 20 points, Horace Grant added 17 and eight rebounds and Penny Hardaway contributed 16 points for the Magic, who managed just 18 fourth-quarter points.

In Indianapolis, Terrell Brandon scored eight of his 22 points in the fourth quarter and had a career-high 12 rebounds and nine assists as the Cleveland Cavaliers allowed just 29 second-half points in an 83-75 victory over the Pacers.
The Cavaliers have won their first two games following the All-Star break after dropping four of five prior to the break.
Reggie Miller scored 22 points and Rik Smits 17 for the Pacers, who were cooled off by the league's top defensive team after winning four of their last five games.

In Phoenix, Wesley Person scored a career-high 33 points and Kevin Johnson registered a triple-double as the Suns exploded for a season high in points with a 131-100 trouncing of the hapless Boston Celtics.
Person shot 13-of-14 from the field. He also made 7-of-8 foul shots.
Johnson scored 22 points and registered season highs in rebounds and assists, totalling 11 and 17, respectively.
Antoine Walker scored a career-high 29 points for the Celtics, who have lost 20 of 22 road games this season.
In San Antonio, Bryant Reeves recorded 31 points and 12 rebounds and Greg Anthony added 24 points and 11 assists as the Vancouver Grizzlies beat the Spurs 106-101.
Shareef Abdur-Rahim chipped in 19 points for Vancouver, which snapped a three-game losing streak and won for only the second time in 13 games.
The Grizzlies are only 4-22 on the road but defeated the Spurs for the third time in four tries this season.
Vernon Maxwell scored 19 points for San Antonio, which has lost seven of its last eight contests and four in a row at home.
